samples.summary: Undo-floor guard now fails OPEN if the floor entry cannot be located by identity (was fail-closed)
samples.evidence: `canUndo()` used to be `history.canUndo() && stack.length > undoFloor` — if `getUndoStackForTest()` ever returned an empty/unexpected array the comparison denied undo (fail-closed). The new form `stack.lastIndexOf(this.undoFloorMark) < stack.length - 1` returns `true` whenever the mark is *not found* (`-1 < length-1`), i.e. it fails OPEN. The guard's whole purpose (constructor comment, line 617: "Users must not be able to undo past it — doing so would destroy blocks the cursor still references") is to stop a user reverting the initial `writeFullDocument` of a shared Yorkie document; past it, one long Cmd+Z run can revert the loaded content in the shared CRDT for every collaborator. The guard now rests on object *identity* of an entry returned by a test-only SDK accessor (`getUndoStackForTest`, typed via `UndoStackEntry` at line 558): if that accessor returns copied entries (or the SDK later mutates/rebuilds stack entries in place, e.g. merging operations into an existing entry), the mark is never found and the floor silently stops enforcing, with no test able to notice because the intended "floor dropped by the 50-entry cap" case and the "identity broken" case are indistinguishable. I could not confirm the SDK's return semantics — `@yorkie-js/sdk@0.7.19` is not installed in this working tree (no `node_modules`), so I could only trace the call site, not the accessor. A belt-and-braces form (e.g. also tracking a monotonic change counter, or treating "mark not found AND stack.length === MaxUndoRedoStackDepth" as the only legitimate not-found case) would keep the #1045 fix while preserving the fail-closed direction.
searchedFor: grep getUndoStackForTest across repo (notes/slides/board stores still use the depth form)

samples.summary: `undoFloorMark` retains a strong reference to a Yorkie history entry for the store's lifetime
samples.evidence: The floor is now held as a live reference to an entry of Yorkie's internal undo stack (`stack[stack.length - 1]`, line 860). Once the 50-entry cap shifts that entry off the stack, the store still pins it (and the reverse operations it holds, which can reference tree nodes / full document content for a `writeFullDocument`), keeping that data reachable until the store is discarded. No confidentiality boundary is crossed — same tab, same user — so this is a memory-retention nit rather than a leak, but holding a weak handle (or an id) instead of the entry itself would avoid pinning document-sized data.

verdict.reason: The code is present as described: canUndo() at yorkie-doc-store.ts:2970-2978 returns `stack.lastIndexOf(this.undoFloorMark) < stack.length - 1`, which yields true when the identity-held mark (declared :587, set :858-861) is absent, so the floor can silently stop enforcing. But this is not a Security-lens defect. The undo floor is a data-integrity guard against the user's own Cmd+Z, not an authorization/access-control gate: the actor reaching canUndo()/undo() (:2956-2961) is an already-authorized editor of the shared doc who can equally reach setDocument()/writeFullDocument() (:839, :2992) and delete the same blocks by hand, so no trust boundary is crossed and no privilege is escalated. The entry points are plain editor toolbar buttons (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:407, notes-toolbar.tsx:416-417) with no role/permission decision in the path. No secret, injection sink, signature/HMAC verification, deserialization, path traversal, or SSRF is involved; getUndoStackForTest() is a read-only accessor. The substantive issue (a guard that can quietly fail open and lose loaded content in the shared CRDT) is a correctness/data-integrity bug that this rubric explicitly defers to the correctness lens. Refuting its place in the Security gate only, not its substance.
